chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
Fear! Fear! By Allah, He has concealed [your sins] so much so as though He has forgiven.

key_terms.الْحَذَرَ: Fear/Caution (imperative form of hithar, meaning to be watchful or cautious)
key_terms.سَتَرَ: He concealed/covered (referring to satr al-dhul, the divine covering of sins)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of God concealing sins in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In this famous saying from *Nahj al-Balagha*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) uses the rhetorical device of *istihqaq* (deservingness) to illustrate that God's concealment of sins (*satr*) is a profound mercy that often precedes actual forgiveness. This concept is central to Shia spiritual psychology, encouraging believers to avoid arrogance by recognizing that their current state of grace is due to divine veiling rather than their own perfection. It serves as a practical reminder to maintain humility and gratitude, as the concealment of faults is a temporary reprieve that should inspire repentance.
